judge: Assistant qualitative review of each NL/CNL pair; not an independent human or automatic semantic oracle
unit: One complete input case; all sentences and speech acts must succeed
success: CNL is intelligible and preserves participants, predicate, negation, modality, quantifier and coordination scope, conditions, time, relative clauses, quoted attribution, speech act and explicit pragmatic material (including please, greetings and interjections). Minor capitalization or contractions alone do not fail.
failure: Any material omission, addition, scope change, wrong speech act, unintelligible construction or runtime error
uncertain: Ambiguity or insufficiently reliable reconstruction; counted as non-success in the reported conservative rate
rate: success / all cases in the split, including runtime failures
limitations: Authored realistic English examples, not sampled production data
Development cases are inspected during tuning
20 holdout cases are rendered and judged only after five rounds
Same assistant authored, repaired and judged; scores are estimates with evaluator bias
Coverage is reported separately and never used as the semantic verdict
Parser attribution is based on inspected dependency structures, not proof of causal exclusivity
